A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RPS and ARGUS research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original entity-retrievability audits, diagnostic-probe evaluations, and downstream retrieval experiments, including additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds augmentation-budget experiments, replacement-only indexing, threshold sensitivity, and augmentation ablations.

M1.justification: The core RPS, diagnostic probes, and ARGUS augmentation pipeline remain unchanged. Section 7.3 adds limited procedural variants: prioritizing the lowest-RPS entities under an augmentation budget and replacing originals with synthesized documents instead of retaining both views.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Wikidata–Wikipedia audit and the same benchmark coverage: 10 BRIGHT domains, two ImpliRet settings, and seven RAR-B subsets. The new analyses use retained data; additional benchmarks discussed in related work are not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds evaluated Untargeted Random KB, Random Entity Augmentation, and All Entities comparators against ARGUS for BGE-M3 and ReasonIR. These substantially extend the comparisons beyond unaugmented indexing and the two ARGUS remedies; the original eight retrievers and probe comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces augmentation budgets of 20–80% plus unrestricted augmentation, a fixed-index-size replacement experiment, and threshold sweeps from 0 to 1. Tables 4–7 evaluate BGE-M3 and ReasonIR on retained benchmark subsets. These are added experimental designs; the original benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Sections 7.3–7.4 examine augmentation density, budget sensitivity, gains without index growth, threshold robustness, and the roles of entity grounding and risk-based selection. Appendix Figure 6 also replaces the eight-retriever visualization with a Reason-Embed grid varying retrieval cutoff and neutral-pool size.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these experiments. The existing calibration and residual diagnostics are retained without changes to uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original appendix tables retain their numerical results, with v1 Tables 3–5 becoming v2 Tables 8–10. New Tables 3–7 add substantial results; for example, Table 5 reports BGE-M3 ImpliRet scores of 23.72 for replacement versus 21.05 for baseline. New entries also contain an unexplained RAR-B discrepancy: BGE-M3 ARGUS scores are 25.53 in Tables 4/7 versus 20.26 at the default threshold in Table 6.

T1.justification: The RPS expectation and empirical hit-rate definitions, pooling equations, and risk-aggregation formulas are unchanged. The expanded discussion of prior theoretical limitations adds research context, not new mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: entity-level RPS auditing, prediction from embeddings, and targeted ARGUS remediation. The abstract also retains the claimed average gains of +3.4 nDCG@5 and +4.5 nDCG@10; the new experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that gains extend beyond index growth, depend on targeted entity selection, and tolerate nearby thresholds. Appendix A adds substantive discussion of exposure bias, KB poisoning, and synthesis hallucinations. The earlier standalone discussion of uniform-configuration limitations is removed, while the conclusion explicitly notes dense-retriever scope and dependence on KB coverage.

D1.justification: Sections 7.3–7.4 document how the new budgets and controls operate, including additional views per original corpus size, lowest-RPS prioritization, and random passage/entity selection. Existing pooling details, probe hyperparameters, NER and synthesis models, prompt, and code/data repository remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The new extended-related-work Appendix A substantially broadens positioning around classical retrievability, entity-centric failures, embedding limitations, document/query expansion, and trustworthy retrieval. It explicitly connects RPS to classical retrievability and distinguishes ARGUS from methods such as doc2query and HyDE, beyond merely adding citations.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order remain. v2 copyedits the method description, revises the results introduction and conclusion, replaces the key-takeaway subsection with expanded analyses, removes the standalone limitations section, and replaces the appendix overview with extended related work. Citation style changes from author–year to numbered references.

P2.justification: v2 adds five tables and substantially replaces Figure 6: eight retriever columns at fixed k=50 become four cutoff columns, k=10/25/50/100, for Reason-Embed. Its caption still describes the previous all-retriever figure. Existing figures and tables are also relocated, including the retained appendix tables renumbered 8–10.

improvement.justification: The new controls address v1's unresolved questions about targeting versus generic expansion, and Appendix A improves research positioning. However, conflicting BGE-M3 RAR-B results across Tables 4, 6, and 7 undermine interpretation of the central new evidence. Figure 6 also replaces the cross-retriever analysis without updating its caption. These substantive benefits and reporting problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
